title: batch-response
description:
What every ingestion endpoint returns.

The four counts are disjoint and together account for every submitted record: accepted + rejected + duplicated + skipped == submitted. A loader can check that arithmetic and know nothing was silently dropped, which is the one thing a bulk import has to be able to establish.

`errors` carries one entry per rejected row, with its index, so a caller can fix the file rather than bisect it. Narratives, secrets and raw identifiers never appear in it.

ok.description: False when anything was rejected, even if the batch was partially applied. A caller that checks only the HTTP status would otherwise treat a half-loaded batch as a success.

duplicated.description: Records whose natural key already existed. Counted apart from rejected, because a re-run of the same file is a normal event and should not read as a failure.

index.description: Position in the submitted array, zero-based.
